questions.question: Who among the following was the last Tirthankara of Jainism?
questions.solution:
Lord Mahavira was the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism.
  • He was a contemporary of Gautama Buddha and attained Kaivalya (enlightenment) at the age of 42.

questions.question: Who was the British Governor-General during the Revolt of 1857?
questions.solution:
Lord Canning was the Governor-General when the Revolt of 1857 broke out.
  • After the revolt, he became the first Viceroy of India under the Government of India Act 1858.

questions.question: Who was the last Mauryan king, killed by his Commander-in-Chief, leading to the establishment of the Shunga dynasty?
questions.solution:
Brihadratha was the last ruler of the Mauryan Empire.
  • He was killed by his general, Pushyamitra Shunga, in 185 BCE.

questions.question: Which group of people settled in northwestern India around Taxila in the 1st century BC?
questions.solution:
The Kushanas, led by the Yuezhi tribe, established a vast empire including Taxila in the 1st century.
  • Their most famous ruler was Kanishka.

questions.question: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 resulted in the partition of India into how many dominions?
questions.solution: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 divided British India into two independent dominions: India and Pakistan.

questions.question: Who was the prominent leader of the Deoband Movement, which aimed to preserve Islamic culture?
questions.solution:
Muhammad Qasim Nanotavi was a primary founder of the Deoband Movement (Darul Uloom Deoband) in 1866.
  • It aimed to revive Islamic learning and oppose Western influence.

questions.question: In which part of India did the earliest iron objects appear in the overlap between the Neolithic and Megalithic phases?
questions.solution: The earliest iron objects in the Neolithic-Megalithic overlap phase (c. 1200 BCE) have been found predominantly in South India, at sites like Hallur.

questions.question: In ancient times, who among the following categorically mentioned that ‘there are 360 bones in a human body’?
questions.solution: In the ancient medical treatise Charaka Samhita, Charaka stated that there are 360 bones in the human body (including teeth and cartilage).

questions.question: In which year was the Indian Press Act, a law that granted the government extensive powers to control the press in India, passed?
questions.solution: The Indian Press Act was passed in 1910 to restrict the freedom of the press and curb the influence of revolutionary nationalist writings.

questions.question: Which Iranian-origin group was known in Indian sources as Shaka-Pahlava?
questions.solution: In ancient Indian history and inscriptions, the Parthians were often referred to as Pahlavas or Shaka-Pahlavas because of their close cultural and political links with the Shakas.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Abhinav Bharat Mandir (Young India Society)?
questions.option_3: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and Ganesh Damodar Savarkar
questions.solution: The Abhinav Bharat Society was a secret revolutionary society founded by Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and his brother Ganesh Savarkar in 1904.

questions.question: Which of the following sites is linked to the Indus Valley Civilisation?
questions.solution:
Mohenjo-Daro is a major site of the Indus Valley Civilisation located in present-day Pakistan.
  • It is famous for the Great Bath and the Bronze Dancing Girl statue.

questions.question: Which revolutionary leader attempted to assassinate Lord Hardinge?
questions.solution: Rash Behari Bose was the mastermind behind the attempt to assassinate Lord Hardinge in 1912 (the Delhi-Lahore Conspiracy Case).

questions.question: The 'Poona Pact' of 1932 was an agreement between which two leaders?
questions.solution:
The Poona Pact (1932) was an agreement between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
  • It abandoned separate electorates for depressed classes but increased reserved seats for them.

questions.question: The Maukharis were originally tributary rulers who later established an independent kingdom in which region?
questions.solution: The Maukharis established their power in the Western Ganges plains, with their capital at Kannauj, following the decline of the Gupta Empire.

questions.question: The period when we find environmental changes, beginning about 12,000 years ago till about 10,000 years ago, is called:
questions.solution: The Mesolithic period (Middle Stone Age) is characterized by environmental changes and the use of small stone tools called Microliths.

questions.question: In which year was the All India Women’s Conference (AIWC) established?
questions.solution: The All India Women’s Conference (AIWC) was established in 1927 by Margaret Cousins to promote women's education and social welfare.
